findings.title: Environment file exposed
findings.description: An environment file is downloadable. These routinely hold database passwords, API keys and signing secrets.
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, block dotfiles, and rotate every secret it contained.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, Content-Type: unknown; expected format detected (contents intentionally not stored)

findings.title: CORS trusts the 'null' origin
findings.description: Sandboxed iframes and local files send `Origin: null`, so trusting it lets an attacker-controlled page read responses cross-origin.
findings.remediation: Never allow the 'null' origin; allow-list specific HTTPS origins.
findings.evidence: Origin: null -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null; Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

findings.title: CORS reflects arbitrary Origin values
findings.description: The server echoes back whatever Origin it receives. Combined with credentials, any website can read authenticated responses on behalf of a logged-in visitor.
findings.remediation: Validate Origin against an explicit allow-list and never reflect it blindly.
findings.evidence: Origin: https://shieldprobe-test.invalid -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://shieldprobe-test.invalid; Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true

findings.title: Git repository exposed
findings.description: The .git directory is web-accessible, which usually allows the full source code and commit history (including past secrets) to be downloaded.
findings.remediation: Block access to dotfiles/.git at the web server and deploy build artifacts only.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, Content-Type: unknown; starts with: ref: refs/heads/main

findings.title: Database dump exposed
findings.description: A SQL dump is downloadable and likely contains user and business data.
findings.remediation: Remove database dumps from the web root; store backups in private storage.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, Content-Type: unknown; expected format detected (contents intentionally not stored)

findings.title: Cookies set without the HttpOnly flag
findings.description: Cookies readable by JavaScript can be stolen through any XSS flaw.
findings.remediation: Add `HttpOnly` to cookies that client-side code does not need to read.

findings.title: Cookies set without the Secure flag
findings.description: Cookies without Secure can be sent over plain HTTP, exposing them to network eavesdroppers.
findings.remediation: Add the `Secure` attribute to every cookie on an HTTPS site.

findings.title: phpinfo() page exposed
findings.description: phpinfo output discloses PHP configuration, paths, modules and environment variables.
findings.remediation: Delete diagnostic scripts from production.
findings.evidence: HTTP 200, Content-Type: unknown; starts with: <html><title>phpinfo()</title>PHP Version 7.2.24</html>

findings.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
findings.description: CSP is the main defence-in-depth control against cross-site scripting and content injection. No policy is enforced on this response.
findings.remediation: Define a restrictive policy, e.g. `default-src 'self'`, and loosen only as needed.

findings.title: Missing clickjacking protection
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is set, so other sites can embed this page in a frame and trick users into clicking hidden controls.
findings.remediation: Send `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'` (and optionally `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` for legacy browsers).

findings.title: Missing Strict-Transport-Security header
findings.description: Without HSTS, browsers may connect over plain HTTP first, which allows SSL-stripping and downgrade attacks on hostile networks.
findings.remediation: Send `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` on all HTTPS responses.

findings.title: Error pages expose internal details
findings.description: A request for a non-existent URL returned debugging output such as stack traces, file paths or database errors, which helps attackers map the application.
findings.remediation: Disable debug mode in production and return generic error pages; log details server-side only.
findings.evidence: HTTP 404: PHP error message with file path detected (response body not stored)

findings.title: Cookies set without a SameSite attribute
findings.description: Without an explicit SameSite value, behaviour depends on browser defaults, which weakens CSRF protection on older clients.
findings.remediation: Set `SameSite=Lax` (or `Strict`) unless cross-site use is required.

findings.title: Missing Referrer-Policy header
findings.description: Full URLs (which can contain tokens or identifiers) may leak to third parties through the Referer header.
findings.remediation: Send `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin` (or stricter).

findings.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.description: Browsers may MIME-sniff responses and execute content as a different type than the server declared.
findings.remediation: Send `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on all responses.

findings.title: HTML generator tag discloses CMS version
findings.description: The page advertises the exact CMS or framework version in a meta tag.
findings.remediation: Remove the generator meta tag (most CMSs offer a setting or filter for this).

findings.title: Server header discloses software version
findings.description: Exact version numbers help attackers match the server to known vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Configure the web server to send a generic or no Server header (e.g. `ServerTokens Prod` on Apache, `server_tokens off;` on nginx).

findings.title: x-powered-by header reveals technology stack
findings.description: Technology and framework banners narrow an attacker's search for applicable exploits.
findings.remediation: Remove the `x-powered-by` response header.

findings.title: No security.txt published
findings.description: A security.txt file tells researchers how to report vulnerabilities responsibly.
findings.remediation: Publish /.well-known/security.txt with a Contact field (see securitytxt.org).

findings.title: Missing Permissions-Policy header
findings.description: Browser features such as camera, microphone and geolocation are not explicitly restricted for this page and its embedded content.
findings.remediation: Send a Permissions-Policy that disables features the site does not use, e.g. `camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`.
